the most important effect is the time dependence of currents, that the most important current is due to the geo-magnetic induction, that the most impor-tant effect of the geo-magnetic in-duction is the current induced by the positive ions, and that the most impoant effect of the positive ions is their induction current.

we have developed a macroscopic model for radio emission from air showers that is based on currents from shower simulations and that we find that the most relevant contribution to the pulse signal is related to the currents, and that for inclined air showers with a sufficiently large impact parameter, the contribution due the currents induced by geo-magnetic field are dominant, but neither charge excess nor dipole contribution can to be neglected.
the time signal from air showers can be calculated from currents obtained from shower simulations in a macroscopic way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the macroscopic description of the radio emission from air showers.
the macroscopic calculation of the coherent electro-magnetic radio emission from air showers initiated in the atmosphere by ultra-high energy (E > 10(17) eV) cosmic rays.
the macroscopic description of coherent radio emission from air showers initiated with ultra-high energy cosmic-rays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radio emission of cosmic ray induced air showers is dominated by the currents induced by a geo-magnetic field, which are in turn dominated by the time variation of currents.
the most important contributions are due to currents in the shower, which are related to the time dependence, the inclination, and the impact parameter of the air shower.
the macroscopic treatment presented in the paper is in agreement with the microscopic treatment presented in the same paper and in the paper by Risse et al. (2008).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to calculate the time dependence of a radio pulse, based on a realistic geo-mag-netic field and a realistic index of refrac-tion.
we have shown that the radio pulse is a superposition of a charge excess pulse, a dipole pulse and a geo-magnetic pulse, the last one being dominant.
the radio signal of a cosmic ray air shower can be calculated from the currents induced on the ground by the shower.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time signal is dominated by the currents.
the signal from the radio emission from air showers is not just a dipole, and that the dipole is a small part of the total signal.
the time structure of the radio signal from air showers is dominated by the currents induced by geomagnetic fields.
